subject: Energy
title: Small Modular Reactors
description: Learn Small Modular Reactors in one minute.

hook.text: Small modular reactors (SMRs) generate 50–300 MW—factory-built in modules, then shipped and assembled on site.

buildup.text: Conventional reactors take 10–15 years to build—SMRs promise 3–5 years by standardizing designs and factory production.

discovery.text: Passive safety systems use gravity and convection—no pumps or power needed to cool the reactor in an emergency.

twist.text: NuScale's US project was canceled in 2023—costs rose to $9.5 billion, undermining the 'cheap and fast' narrative.

climax.text: Russia and China already operate SMR-like reactors—while Western projects remain largely on paper.

punchline.text: Smaller, faster, safer—SMRs sound great, but costs must fall.

quiz.question: What happened to NuScale's US SMR project in 2023?
options: It was canceled due to rising costs
